gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states the extender's body size against a 13-inch laptop's lid: Mobile Pixels lists its 13.3-inch Duex Plus at 12.25 × 8.46 in, and Apple lists the 13-inch MacBook Air at 11.97 × 8.46 in, so it is the same height and 0.28 in (7 mm) wider.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides.com (cited) and lbdsoftware.com (cited); techpp.com (cited) returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so this score is provisional. itechguides already gives the fit in laptop inches (Duex Plus DS for 13- to 14-inch laptops, Duex Max DS for 'roughly 14 inches or larger') but no dimensions for any product and no weight for either Duex DS. lbdsoftware already says a 14.2-inch single extender rules out 'a 13-inch MacBook Air or a small XPS', and gives only thickness, no width or height. Neither page puts an extender's width and height beside a laptop lid's. The finding is held at 1 because the Mobile Pixels spec page I opened is titled 'DUEX Plus' and does not say it covers the current DS version.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's pick on size: the 13.3-inch Duex Plus DS is the single-screen extender whose body matches a 13-inch lid. It is not one of our linked records, but it is sold on the same Mobile Pixels (cj:mobilepixels) store page as our Duex Max DS, so it can be linked. Our own rows are at risk: itechguides relays the 14.1-inch Duex Max DS as for laptops 'roughly 14 inches or larger', and I could not open a maker fit range for the FOPO S1 or S7. If neither maker states 13 inches in its range, the page has fewer than two fitting rows from our list and should be skipped under the page rules. On video path, Mobile Pixels states the Duex DS needs no driver over USB-C or Mini HDMI, so one added screen stays within what a 13-inch MacBook Air (M4) drives.
